1.title: Quick Reference Recap and Pattern Chooser
1.text: Welcome to Module sixteen: Quick Reference Recap and Pattern Chooser. This module covers quick-reference recap and pattern chooser. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. A symptom-to-fix chooser for every domain. The exact names, flags and values that questions use. The distractor patterns and the rule that defeats each.

1.title: Case Check-In: Birchwood Supply
1.text: Our running case is Birchwood Supply. Birchwood Supply. The solution architect meets the topic of this module. Your job: decide, step by step, which design choice fits.

1.title: Domain 1: Agentic Architecture and Orchestration (27%)
1.text: Domain one: Agentic Architecture and Orchestration (twenty-seven percent). Loop never ends or ends too soon. The best answer is...: Stop on end turn, continue on tool use; no text parsing, no iteration cap as main stop. Module: one. A mandatory step is skipped (verify before refund). The best answer is...: Programmatic prerequisite gate or hook. Module: three. A business limit must always hold. The best answer is...: Interception hook that blocks and redirects. Module: three. Tool results come in mixed formats. The best answer is...: Post Tool Use normalization hook. Module: three. Escalation arrives without context. The best answer is...: Structured handoff summary. Module: three. Report misses a whole area, subagents "succeeded". The best answer is...: Fix the coordinator's decomposition. Module: two.

1.title: Domain 1: Agentic Architecture and Orchestration (27%), continued
1.text: Domain one: Agentic Architecture and Orchestration (twenty-seven percent), continued. Subagent output lacks sources. The best answer is...: Pass findings plus metadata in the prompt. Module: two. Independent searches are slow. The best answer is...: Several Task calls in one response. Module: two. twelve-file review is uneven and contradictory. The best answer is...: Per-file passes plus integration pass. Module: four. Unfamiliar legacy task. The best answer is...: Dynamic decomposition: map, prioritize, adapt. Module: four. Resume after files changed. The best answer is...: Resume plus tell it which files changed; stale to fresh summary. Module: four. Compare two approaches from one analysis. The best answer is...: fork session. Module: four.

1.title: Domain 2: Tool Design and MCP Integration (18%)
1.text: Domain two: Tool Design and M C P (Model Context Protocol) Integration (eighteen percent). Wrong tool among similar ones. The best answer is...: Richer descriptions (formats, examples, edge cases, boundaries) first. Module: five. Two tools overlap. The best answer is...: Rename plus rewrite, or split into purpose-specific tools. Module: five. Agent cannot tell failure types. The best answer is...: Structured errors: category, is Retryable, message. Module: five. Timeout versus no results confused. The best answer is...: Failure equals error; no matches equals valid empty success. Module: five. Agent has eighteen tools and misuses them. The best answer is...: Scope tools to roles (four to five). Module: six. Frequent small need in another role. The best answer is...: Scoped cross-role tool (verify fact). Module: six. Must call a tool, any one. The best answer is...: tool choice: "any". Module: six.

1.title: Domain 2: Tool Design and MCP Integration (18%), continued
1.text: Domain two: Tool Design and M C P Integration (eighteen percent), continued. A given tool must run first. The best answer is...: Forced tool selection. Module: six. Share a server with the team. The best answer is...: Project dot M C P dot Jason plus the env variable. Module: six. Personal experimental server. The best answer is...: User home dot Claude dot json. Module: six. Search content or find files or edit unique text. The best answer is...: Grep or Glob or Edit; no unique anchor to Read plus Write. Module: six.

1.title: Domain 3: Claude Code Configuration and Workflows (20%)
1.text: Domain three: Claude Code Configuration and Workflows (twenty percent). Teammate misses standards. The best answer is...: Move from user to project Claude dot M D. Module: seven. Huge Claude dot M D. The best answer is...: the dot Claude rules folder files, the at import syntax. Module: seven. What did it load? The best answer is...: slash memory. Module: seven. Shared command. The best answer is...: the dot Claude commands folder. Module: seven. Verbose skill output. The best answer is...: context: fork. Module: seven. Ask for parameters. The best answer is...: argument-hint. Module: seven. Conventions by file type, spread out. The best answer is...: the dot Claude rules folder with paths: globs. Module: seven. Big multi-file change. The best answer is...: Plan mode, then execute. Module: eight. Small, clear fix. The best answer is...: Direct execution. Module: eight. Prose misunderstood. The best answer is...: two to three examples; tests first; interview pattern. Module: eight. C I hangs. The best answer is...: dash p. Module: eight. C I needs machine-readable output. The best answer is...: dash dash output format json plus dash dash json schema. Module: eight.

1.title: Domain 3: Claude Code Configuration and Workflows (20%), continued
1.text: Domain three: Claude Code Configuration and Workflows (twenty percent), continued. Duplicate review comments. The best answer is...: Pass prior findings. Module: eight. Self-review finds nothing. The best answer is...: Independent instance. Module: eight, eleven.

1.title: Domain 4: Prompt Engineering and Structured Output (20%)
1.text: Domain four: Prompt Engineering and Structured Output (twenty percent). Too many false positives. The best answer is...: Explicit report or skip criteria (not "be conservative"); disable noisy category meanwhile. Module: nine. Inconsistent severity. The best answer is...: Severity levels with code examples. Module: nine. Inconsistent format or ambiguous cases. The best answer is...: two to four few-shot examples with reasoning. Module: nine. Broken Jason (Java Script Object Notation). The best answer is...: Tool use plus Jason schema. Module: ten. Fabricated values. The best answer is...: Nullable or optional fields. Module: ten. New categories appear. The best answer is...: Enum plus other plus detail; unclear. Module: ten. Totals do not add up. The best answer is...: Validation; calculated total versus stated total. Module: ten. Validation failed. The best answer is...: Retry with document plus failure plus errors; none if the info is absent. Module: ten.

1.title: Domain 4: Prompt Engineering and Structured Output (20%), continued
1.text: Domain four: Prompt Engineering and Structured Output (twenty percent), continued. Cheap nightly job. The best answer is...: Batch A P I (application programming interface) (fifty percent, up to twenty-four h, custom id); never for blocking work. Module: eleven. S L A (service level agreement) planning. The best answer is...: Interval plus twenty-four h at most S L A. Module: eleven.

1.title: Domain 5: Context Management and Reliability (15%)
1.text: Domain five: Context Management and Reliability (fifteen percent). Amounts or dates vanish in long chats. The best answer is...: Case-facts block outside summaries. Module: twelve. Findings in the middle are missed. The best answer is...: Key summary first, section headers. Module: twelve. Tool output bloat. The best answer is...: Trim to relevant fields. Module: twelve. "Typical patterns" in long exploration. The best answer is...: Scratchpad, subagents, manifest, slash compact. Module: twelve. Wrong escalations. The best answer is...: Explicit criteria plus few-shot; not sentiment or confidence. Module: thirteen. Customer asks for a person. The best answer is...: Escalate now. Module: thirteen. Several matches. The best answer is...: Ask for another identifier. Module: thirteen. Subagent failure. The best answer is...: Structured error context, partial results, coverage annotations. Module: thirteen. ninety-seven percent accuracy overall. The best answer is...: Per-type, per-field accuracy; stratified sampling; calibrated confidence. Module: fourteen.

1.title: Domain 5: Context Management and Reliability (15%), continued
1.text: Domain five: Context Management and Reliability (fifteen percent), continued. Conflicting statistics. The best answer is...: Both values, with sources and dates. Module: fourteen. Exam tip: Read the last sentence of the stem first, name the symptom, then match it to a row of this chooser.

1.title: Names and Values to Know Exactly
1.text: Names and Values to Know Exactly. Loop signals. stop reason: tool use (continue), end turn (stop). tool choice. "auto", "any", {"type":"tool","name":"..."}. Spawning. Task tool (now Agent); allowed Tools includes it; Agent Definition. Hooks. Post Tool Use (results), call interception (Pre Tool Use in current docs). M C P. is Error; dot M C P dot Jason (project) and home dot Claude dot json (user); the github token variable. Built-ins. Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob. Claude dot M D. home dot Claude, Claude dot M D, Claude dot M D or the dot Claude Claude dot M D file, subdirectory files, the dot Claude rules folder, the at import syntax, slash memory. Commands or skills. the dot Claude commands folder, home dot Claude commands, a skill folder with a Skill dot M D file, context: fork, allowed-tools, argument-hint. Rule frontmatter. paths: with globs (any test T S X file, anything under terraform). C L I (command-line interface). dash p or dash dash print, dash dash output format json, dash dash json schema, dash dash resume less than name greater than, dash dash fork session.

1.title: Names and Values to Know Exactly, continued
1.text: Names and Values to Know Exactly, continued. Batches. fifty percent, up to twenty-four h, custom id, no multi-turn tool calling. Error metadata. error Category (transient or validation or permission or business), is Retryable. Self-check fields. calculated total, stated total, conflict detected, detected pattern. Exam. sixty items, one hundred twenty min, seven hundred twenty or one thousand, four of six scenarios. Exam tip: Exact names matter: stop reason, tool choice, dot M C P dot Jason, context: fork, paths:, dash p, dash dash json schema.

1.title: Distractor Patterns and the Rule That Beats Them
1.text: Distractor Patterns and the Rule That Beats Them. "Strengthen the prompt" for a hard requirement. Why it is wrong: Probabilistic. Rule: one. "Add a classifier or routing layer" first. Why it is wrong: Over-engineered before simple fixes. Rule: three. "Self-reported confidence" or "sentiment" as the trigger. Why it is wrong: Poor proxies. Rule: six. "Blame the downstream agent". Why it is wrong: Logs point upstream. Rule: two. "Give every agent all tools". Why it is wrong: No least privilege. Rule: four. "Generic error message or empty success". Why it is wrong: Hides recovery information. Rule: five, nine. "Abort the whole run". Why it is wrong: Wastes partial results. Rule: nine. "Use the bigger context window". Why it is wrong: Attention quality is the issue. Rule: seven. "Batch for everything (fifty percent off)". Why it is wrong: No latency guarantee. Rule: eight. "Same session reviews itself". Why it is wrong: Keeps its reasoning. Rule: seven.

1.title: Distractor Patterns and the Rule That Beats Them, continued
1.text: Distractor Patterns and the Rule That Beats Them, continued. "Read everything up front". Why it is wrong: Burns context. Rule: ten. Exam tip: A distractor is wrong because it is probabilistic, over-engineered, hiding information, over-privileged or mistimed.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Order of study: D one first (twenty-seven percent), then D three and D four (twenty percent each), D two (eighteen percent), D five (fifteen percent). Core stance: Deterministic, root-cause, proportionate, least privilege, structured, independent, latency-matched, no silent failure, context-aware. Day before: Reread this module and the ten rules in Module zero. In the next module, we continue the course.
